name: oc-time-report
description: Estimation-vs-logged-hours report over a period (independent of the AI-usage JSON). Tempo-worklog driven and TICKET-based with PER-AREA columns. Tickets are selected by their DATE (resolutiondate, else updated) in the window, and every worklog on a selected ticket counts (all-time, so per-ticket totals match Jira's aggregatetimespent). One row per ticket with a column group for each area (Backend/Frontend/QA) giving that area's main developer, Architect & Dev-lead estimates, total dev / logged / sub-bug hours, an AI flag, two time gains (Architect and Dev-lead, each with/without sub-bugs) and a sub-bug count; a single Arch-gain B/F/Q column (considering bugs) and a Logged+bug B/F/Q/OH column right after the Final flag; and closing Overhead h / Overhead people / Total log h columns. Overhead people (Architect/PO/DevOps/Consultant/management, roster area 'overhead') never count as an area developer — their hours go to the Overhead bucket, itemised per person with hours. Each area's main developer is its top contributor by dev-logged + own sub-bug-fixing hours (a token reviewer never wins). Every ticket carries a Date (resolutiondate, else updated) and is grouped by month; the HTML splits into five tabs (All, User Stories All, User Stories Final, Bugs Final, Bugs and Others), each with Totals-by-area overall + per month and the per-ticket matrix grouped by month. Totals-by-area (shown in days, 1 d = 8 h) add a Project column and a % Logged share column, and the HTML has an interactive Project-filter picklist that live-recomputes the Totals and filters the per-ticket rows. Tempo is fetched with a persistent month-bucketed cache (only the recent ~45 days re-fetched each run). Also writes a second finished-User-Story per-developer summary (per area main dev, split by AI true/false, grouped by month). The roster is embedded (accountId -> name/area/role/active). HTML + CSV to ./docs/, named with the run date and the window start and end (time-report-<date>-<start>-<end>.{html,csv}). Jira via direct REST and Tempo per-user, both mandatory tokens; no Atlassian MCP.
